rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something free of dirt, and it also describes a neat, precise result such as a clean cut.

example.english: This knife makes a clean cut.
example.jyutping: ni1 baa2 dou1 cit3 dak1 hou2 gon1 zeng6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when you mean to remove dirt and make something clean.

example.english: I want to clean the kitchen completely.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 zoeng1 cyu4 fong2 zing2 gon1 zing6

rows.note: Use this when cleaning by wiping a surface or object.

example.english: Please help me clean the table by wiping it.
example.traditional: 你幫我將張枱抹乾淨吖。
example.jyutping: nei5 bong1 ngo5 zoeng1 zoeng1 toi2 mut3 gon1 zing6 aa1

rows.note: Use this mainly for cleaning a place, especially by sweeping or doing household cleaning.

example.english: I clean the whole flat every morning.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 daa2 sou3 saai3 seng4 gaan1 uk1

rows.note: Use this when the main idea is putting a room or area in order rather than removing dirt.

example.english: Remember to clean up the table after dinner.
example.jyutping: sik6 jyun4 faan6 gei3 dak1 zap1 sap6 zoeng1 toi2

rows.note: Use 型 when “clean” means cool or stylish, especially when praising someone's clothes or shoes.

example.jyutping: nei5 deoi3 bo1 haai4 zan1 hai6 hou2 jing4

rows.note: Use 清白 for moral purity and for an unblemished record, though everyday speech often says 冇案底 for a criminal record.

example.english: I can prove that I am clean.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ho2 ji5 zing3 ming4 zi6 gei2 cing1 baak6

rows.note: Use 空白 when a page or other surface is blank and unmarked.

example.jyutping: ni1 jip6 zung6 hai6 hung1 baak6
